days.title: Warm-up shapes and doodles
days.description: Fill a page with basic shapes, loops, and doodles to loosen up your hand before lettering.
days.tip: Warm-ups matter — cold hands produce shaky, tense letterforms

days.title: Faux calligraphy technique
days.description: Write a word in normal handwriting, then thicken every downstroke to fake a calligraphy look.
days.tip: Faux calligraphy is the fastest way to get the calligraphy look without special tools

days.title: Simple serif alphabet
days.description: Draw the full alphabet in a basic serif style, focusing on consistent letter height.
days.tip: Sketch letters lightly in pencil first, then go over them with your final line

days.title: Simple sans-serif alphabet
days.description: Draw the full alphabet in a bold, blocky sans-serif style.
days.tip: Bold sans-serif letters read best when the strokes are all a uniform thickness

days.title: Banners and flourishes
days.description: Learn to draw a simple ribbon banner and add flourish lines around a lettered word.
days.tip: Draw the banner first, then fit your lettering inside it — not the other way around

days.title: Compose a quote layout
days.description: Lay out a short quote mixing 2 of the styles you have practiced, with a banner or flourish.
days.tip: Mix at most 2-3 lettering styles per piece — more than that looks cluttered

days.title: Week 1 review
days.description: Photograph your favorite piece from the week and note what felt hardest to control.
days.tip: Save every practice page — you will love seeing the before/after in a month
